choices.content: The numbers of participants on both sides are equal
Both players have equal probabilities of winning
Both players have a chance of winning
The game always ends in a draw

question.prompt: Which of the following describes a game that is fair to both players?

solutions.explanation: A game is fair when both players have equal probabilities of winning. Merely having a chance of winning does not necessarily make the game fair. Option B states this fairness criterion. However, under D the game always ends in a draw, so each player's probability of winning is \(0\), and these probabilities are equal. The question does not require either player to have a positive chance of winning. Therefore both B and D satisfy the criterion, so there is no unique single-choice answer.
solutions.title: Apply the fairness criterion to both options
